newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco Bay area home sales decline - report.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco Bay area home sales decline - report.

text.p: San Francisco Bay area home sales declined slightly in September for the first time in over a year, according to a report Wednesday.

A total of 4,504 resale houses were sold in the nine-county Bay area in September, down 22.7 percent from 5,830 for August and down 1.3 percent from 4,561 for September last year, DataQuick Information Systems said.
The decline from August to September is normal for the season, DataQuick said. The year-over-year decline was the first since July 1995 when year-over-year sales declined 14.8 percent.

"The Bay Area is still in a strong sales surge, but rising sales counts inevitably level off. Bay Area price trends are certainly the envy of the rest of California," said Donald L. Cohn, DataQuick's chief executive officer.

The median price paid for a resale house was $236,000 in September, up 2.6 percent from the same month a year ago. Home prices have increased every month this year, and have regained most of the value lost during the early 1990s, DataQuick said.

Sales in other home categories were also up last month. Sales of newly-built homes have been up since October last year, DataQuick reported. DataQuick monitors real estate purchasing and financing nationwide.
